OpenTelemetry traces and metrics in the Supabase .NET SDK

Oct 14, 2026

New Feature

What's new#

The .NET SDK emit traces and metrics through System.Diagnostics. Each client exposes its own ActivitySource and Meter, so you subscribe to them the same way you subscribe to any other .NET instrumentation. The SDK takes no dependency on the OpenTelemetry packages, and the clients stay silent until something subscribes, so there is no overhead when you are not collecting.

This covers the Auth, Postgrest, Storage, and Functions clients. Realtime is not yet instrumented. URLs are recorded with the query string stripped, and no token, credential, or payload is placed in a tag.

What you get#

ClientSpansMetrics
PostgrestOne per request ({METHOD} {path}), with a db.operation tag (select, insert, update, upsert, delete, count, rpc) to tell apart operations that share an HTTP verbsupabase.postgrest.http.request.duration
AuthOne per operation (gotrue.sign_in, gotrue.refresh_token, …), with a child span for the HTTP callsupabase.gotrue.http.request.duration
StorageOne per request, with a storage.transfer.direction tag on uploads and downloads; a resumable (TUS) upload is a single span for the whole transfersupabase.storage.http.request.duration, supabase.storage.transfer.duration, supabase.storage.transfer.size
FunctionsOne per invocation, with a faas.invoked_name tag; a relay error is a failed span even when the HTTP status succeedssupabase.functions.invoke.duration

How to use it#

Add the OpenTelemetry hosting package and an exporter alongside the SDK:


_10
<PackageReference Include="Supabase" Version="8.0.0" />
_10
<PackageReference Include="OpenTelemetry.Extensions.Hosting" Version="1.19.1" />
_10
<PackageReference Include="OpenTelemetry.Exporter.OpenTelemetryProtocol" Version="1.19.1" />

Then register the Supabase sources. Each client shares one name between its ActivitySource and its Meter, so you can register them all at once with SupabaseDiagnostics.SourceNames, or one client at a time by its own SourceName:


_20
using OpenTelemetry.Metrics;
_20
using OpenTelemetry.Trace;
_20
using Supabase;
_20
using Supabase.Postgrest;
_20
using Supabase.Gotrue;
_20
using Supabase.Storage;
_20
using Supabase.Functions;
_20
_20
builder.Services.AddOpenTelemetry()
_20
// All sources at once.
_20
.WithTracing(tracing => tracing
_20
.AddSource(SupabaseDiagnostics.SourceNames.ToArray())
_20
.AddOtlpExporter())
_20
// Or one client at a time.
_20
.WithMetrics(metrics => metrics
_20
.AddMeter(PostgrestDiagnostics.SourceName)
_20
.AddMeter(GotrueDiagnostics.SourceName)
_20
.AddMeter(StorageDiagnostics.SourceName)
_20
.AddMeter(FunctionsDiagnostics.SourceName)
_20
.AddOtlpExporter());

Swap AddOtlpExporter for AddConsoleExporter to print locally, or use any other exporter. Without the OpenTelemetry SDK, a raw ActivityListener or MeterListener works too. We have one README per-package which shows how to do it.

Why it matters#

You get the SDK's calls in the same traces as the rest of your app: which ran, how long they took, whether they failed. You write no instrumentation for it, and the SDK pulls in no OpenTelemetry dependency of its own.

An outdated subset of TLS 1.2 ciphers will be disabled on project HTTP APIs

Oct 12, 2026

Breaking Change

What is being deprecated#

Most users won't notice any change. Starting November 10, 2026 at the earliest, Supabase will stop offering some outdated TLS configurations on project HTTP APIs (<ref>.supabase.co and custom domains). Users on old, unsupported operating systems, or embedded devices that haven't been updated, may lose access if their device only supports the configurations being removed.

The configurations being removed are four CBC-mode TLS 1.2 cipher suites. Cipher suites determine how a connection is encrypted. These older suites have known security weaknesses and often trigger warnings in security scans. We plan to stop offering these ciphers on TLS 1.2:

  • TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_128_CBC_SHA256 (ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-SHA256)
  • TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_CBC_SHA256 (ECDHE-RSA-AES128-SHA256)
  • TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_256_CBC_SHA384 (ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-SHA384)
  • TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_CBC_SHA384 (ECDHE-RSA-AES256-SHA384)

Supabase has only supported TLS 1.2 and 1.3 for several years. There is no change for TLS 1.3.

Auth, the Data API, Storage, Realtime, and Edge Functions are all sub-routes of the Supabase HTTP API, so all five are affected. Direct Postgres connections, pooler connections, and the Management API are not.

Timeline#

DateMilestone
October 12, 2026Deprecation notice published
October 14, 2026Affected customers notified by email
November 10, 2026 at the earliestCBC-mode ciphers removed

Owners of projects that received connections using these deprecated ciphers are being contacted directly with details about the potential impact to their project. If you have any concerns about the impact to your project, please open a support ticket.

What to migrate to#

In the past 30 days, fewer than 0.0001% of connections to Supabase projects negotiated these ciphers, so we expect little to no impact. Devices that only support them are running end-of-life software, such as old operating system installations or embedded products that no longer get updates.

The ciphers offered on TLS 1.2 going forward are:

  • TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 (ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256)
  • TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256 (ECDHE-ECDSA-CHACHA20-POLY1305)
  • TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 (ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256)
  • TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256 (ECDHE-RSA-CHACHA20-POLY1305)
  • TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 (ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384)
  • TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 (ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384)

Migration steps#

  1. Find any client that connects to your project over HTTPS and runs on an end-of-life operating system, an old browser, or an embedded device.
  2. Update that client's operating system or TLS library to a supported version so it supports at least one of the ciphers listed above, or TLS 1.3. Your preferred AI agent or the community around your tech stack may be able to help.
  3. If you're concerned about the impact on your users or need help preparing, open a support ticket and tell us which client and ciphers it needs.

Read more in the TLS docs.

ASP.NET Core dependency injection for the Supabase .NET SDK

Oct 12, 2026

New Feature

What's new#

Supabase.Extensions.DependencyInjection is a new package that provides an easier way to plug the Supabase .NET SDK into your application. It exposes a new method on IServiceCollection called AddSupabase which registers the main client and all sub-clients:


_10
builder.Services.AddSupabase(
_10
supabaseUrl: "https://xyz.supabase.co",
_10
supabaseKey: builder.Configuration["Supabase:Key"]!,
_10
configureOptions: options =>
_10
{
_10
options.AutoConnectRealtime = true;
_10
options.PostgrestRetry = new RetryOptions { MaxRetries = 3 };
_10
});

It registers all clients (Supabase.Client, IGotrueClient, IPostgrestClient, IStorageClient, IFunctionsClient, IRealtimeClient) with a scoped lifecycle, so you can resolve them wherever you need them:


_10
app.MapGet("/movies", async (IPostgrestClient postgrest) =>
_10
await postgrest.Table<Movie>().Get());

The package is available on NuGet:


_10
dotnet add package Supabase.Extensions.DependencyInjection

Why it matters#

You can always register all the required clients in IServiceCollection yourself. This package simply does it all for you and removes boilerplate from your codebase.
